Long table of correlations: one row per pair, with CI, raw and adjusted p

Source: R/tables.R
tbl_cor_long.Rd

Works for cor_cross() / plot_cor_cross() outputs (rows grouped by the family of the adjustment) and for cor_test_matrix() outputs (all pairs). Rows with an adjusted p below alpha are in bold.

Usage

tbl_cor_long(
  x,
  labels = NULL,
  digits = 2,
  alpha = 0.05,
  palette = COR_PAL,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  sort_by = c("none", "abs")
)

Arguments

x

output of cor_cross(), plot_cor_cross() or cor_test_matrix()

labels

named vector variable -> label

digits

decimals of the coefficients

alpha

threshold for bold rows

palette

colours (named low / high) of the coefficient column; NULL = no colour

title, subtitle

override the automatic texts

sort_by

"none" (order of the variables) or "abs" (decreasing |coefficient| within groups)

Value

a gt_tbl

Examples

d  <- simulate_cor_data(150)
cm <- cor_test_matrix(d, c("CRP", "IL6", "BDNF", "BIN_CRP"))
tbl_cor_long(cm, labels = attr(d, "labels"))

Pair: cont = continuous, bin = binary[0/1]. Bold = adjusted p < 0.05.
    
Adjusted p, Benjamini-Hochberg (FDR) over the 6 distinct pairs: * < 0.05, ** < 0.01, *** < 0.001; no star = adjusted p ≥ 0.05.
    
Continuous: r_s = cov(rank_x, rank_y) / (SD(rank_x) × SD(rank_y)); t-test, n − 2 df.
    
95% CI: Fisher z transformation, SE = √(1.06 / (n − 3)) (Fieller et al. 1957); computed with correlation::cor_to_ci() {correlation}.
    
Binary [0/1]: r_s = r_rb × √(3pq), r_rb = 2 AUC − 1 (rank-biserial, ≡ Mann-Whitney test), p, q = group proportions; |r_s| ≤ 0.87, not comparable with continuous pairs.
    
Notation: Makowski D, Ben-Shachar MS, Patil I, Lüdecke D (2020), J Open Source Softw 5(51):2306, doi:10.21105/joss.02306.
